newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin snubs parliament by summoning ministers.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin snubs parliament by summoning ministers.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, snubbing the opposition-dominated parliament, summoned Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and two top ministers to the Kremlin on Wednesday although they had been expected to spend the day before legislators.
Gennady Seleznyov, speaker of the State Duma, or lower house of parliament, announced the summons while Chernomyrdin was answering questions from deputies over the 1997 budget.

The reason for Yeltsin's summons was not immediately known but Itar-Tass news agency said he wanted Chernomyrdin, Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov to take part in a ceremony honouring cellist Mstislav Rostropovich.
The ministers left the hall, but some officials said Chernomyrdin did not leave the building and only telephoned Yeltsin. Chubais returned to the Duma quickly.
The government is trying to persuade the conservative Duma to agree to its proposals to cut budget spending across the board and many ministers were attending the parliament session.
